tasks.title: Ten QPACK static-table entries are truncated at the RFC's line wrap, and the --check that exists to prevent this re-derives the same wrong table
tasks.evidence-before: The committed table holds `{"accept", "application/dns-"}` (:60), `{"content-type", "text/html;"}` (:82), `{"strict-transport-security", "max-age=31536000;"}` (:87,:88), `{"content-security-policy", "script-src 'none';"}` (:115) — also indices 41,44,45,47,54. RFC 9204 Appendix A prints those cells wrapped ("Any line breaks that appear within field names or values are due to formatting"). The extractor matches only rows whose first column is a number (tests/vectors/extract_rfc9204_static_table.py:42,63-66), so it drops the continuation line; `python3 tests/vectors/extract_rfc9204_static_table.py <rfc9204.txt> --check` prints 'rfc9204 static table: committed entries match the RFC' and exits 0 on the defective table. wt_qpack_static_entry is what INDEXED_STATIC/LITERAL_NAME_REF_STATIC decode through (src/http3/qpack_field_section.c), so a peer's static index 52 decodes as `content-type: text/html;`.
tasks.expected: The ten values are the RFC's full cells: application/dns-message (30,44), public, max-age=31536000 (41), application/javascript (45), application/x-www-form-urlencoded (47), text/html; charset=utf-8 (52), text/plain;charset=utf-8 (54), max-age=31536000; includesubdomains (57), max-age=31536000; includesubdomains; preload (58), script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none' (85).
tasks.evidence-after: All ten wrapped static-table entries restored to RFC 9204's full values; the extractor now joins a physically wrapped row instead of dropping it, and --check genuinely fails on a perturbed table (exit 1) where it previously passed. New test test_wrapped_entries_are_full; fails before (20 of 81 checks), passes after; all 99 entries re-verified against the RFC XML; ctest 97/97 and check-vectors.sh exit 0.

tasks.title: The stream-table reclaim decrements the opened-stream counters, so a session reuses stream IDs and then fails to open streams at all
tasks.evidence-before: src/quic/stream.c:459-463 reclaims every complete stream when the 32-slot table is full and does `(*opened)--` per slot; src/quic/connection.c:2305 derives the next stream ID from exactly that counter (`index = wt_quic_stream_table_opened_by_us(...)`), under the comment at :2303-2304 'so it is never reused'. After the first reclaim the counter no longer names the next index: the next open rebuilds a live ID (table_open returns WT_ERR_STATE) or an ID that was already used and finished (RFC 9000 2.1: 'A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a stream ID'). wt_quic_stream_table_close has no caller in src/ or apps/, so the sweep runs on the 33rd open; grep -rn reclaim C99/tests is empty.
tasks.expected: opened_by_us_*/opened_by_peer_* are monotonic counters of IDs issued; reclaim may free used[i] and count but must not decrement them.
tasks.evidence-after: Removed the (*opened)-- from the reclaim path; the four opened counters are documented as monotonic ID issuers. New test test_stream_table_reclaim_keeps_ids_new fails before the fix (want 33, got 1; 'its number is one no earlier stream used' false; 3 of 467 checks FAILED) and passes after; full ctest 97/97.

tasks.title: CONNECT-stream capsule reader hides an unbounded, peer-controlled buffer: remote memory exhaustion
tasks.evidence-before: receiveConnectCapsules (807-850): `var buffered = initialBytes` then `let received = try await stream.receive(atMost: 8_192); buffered.append(received.content)` (831) in a loop. popCompleteCapsule (852-877) decodes the capsule length from the peer: `let payloadLength = try QUICVarInt.decode(from: &cursor)` and rejects only `payloadLength > UInt64(Int.max)`; `guard buffer.count >= capsuleLength else { return nil }` keeps accumulating until the whole declared capsule arrives. The 1024-byte WT_CLOSE_SESSION cap is enforced only later, after buffering (WebTransportFlowControl.swift:169). Each read also re-opens QUIC flow-control credit, so a peer can stream indefinitely; the shipped default bind is non-loopback (WebTransport.swift:101 `localOnly: Bool = false`).
tasks.expected: A declared capsule length above the largest legal CONNECT-stream capsule is rejected before any buffering, and a partial capsule that exceeds the bound resets the stream with H3_MESSAGE_ERROR.
tasks.fix-summary: Added maximumConnectStreamCapsulePayloadBytes (= WT_CLOSE_SESSION's 4-byte code + the draft's 1024-byte message cap = 1028) and a guard in popCompleteCapsule that throws BEFORE buffering when the peer's declared capsule payload exceeds it; the existing catch turns it into an H3_MESSAGE_ERROR stream reset. popCompleteCapsule made internal for direct testing.
tasks.evidence-after: New test WebTransportConnectStreamCapsuleBoundTests (2 tests): FAILS before the fix ('an error was expected but none was thrown'), PASSES after. swift build --build-tests exit 0; swift test exit 0 with 310 tests, 0 failures (was 308); check-manifest-sync.sh OK; swift format lint clean; warning count unchanged (4 pre-existing #UnnecessaryUnsafe lines at 699-700). Ledger note: the bound also refuses unknown/grease capsules larger than 1028 bytes, which RFC 9297 would prefer to ignore -- recorded as residual doubt because this reader does not stream-discard.

tasks.title: On Windows the monotonic clock wraps after about 21 days of uptime because ticks are multiplied by 10^6 before the division
tasks.evidence-before: time.c:35 `return ((uint64_t)counter.QuadPart * 1000000U) / frequency;` overflows uint64 once the tick count passes 2^64/10^6 ~ 1.84e13, i.e. about 21.4 days at the usual 10 MHz QueryPerformanceFrequency (minutes to hours where QPC reports the TSC frequency). After the wrap the value decreases, breaking the monotonicity the file's own header promises and mis-arming every QUIC deadline, idle timeout and PTO. The POSIX branch (time.c:24-27) is unaffected.
tasks.expected: Divide first: (counter / frequency) * 1000000 + ((counter % frequency) * 1000000) / frequency.

tasks.title: waitForReady leaks its checked continuation and connection observer when the handshake times out
tasks.evidence-before: waitForReady (1727-1802) parks `try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in ... connection.onStateUpdate { _, state in handleState(state) } ... }` (1752, 1790) inside `withTimeout(1751)`. handleState (1754-1781) is the only path that resumes the inner continuation. withTimeout's expiry path (1978-1984) does `operationTask.cancel()` and resumes only its own outer continuation; `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` does not resume on cancellation, and there is no withTaskCancellationHandler. The abandoned task therefore stays suspended on an unresumed continuation, retaining the observer closure and role until the connection independently reaches .failed/.cancelled, or forever.
tasks.expected: The inner continuation is resumed exactly once on every path including timeout/cancellation, and the state observer does not outlive the wait.
tasks.fix-summary: waitForReady now wraps its checked continuation in an async withTaskCancellationHandler and resumes it with the timeout error from onCancel, so withTimeout's expiry no longer abandons a task suspended on an unresumed continuation. A new Mutex-backed InteroperableQUICWaitGate makes the observer resume and the cancellation resume mutually exclusive and also handles the cancellation arriving before the continuation is parked. New WebTransportWaitForReadyTests regression test.
tasks.evidence-after: New test WebTransportWaitForReadyTests: FAILS before the fix ('Expectation failed: weakMarker == nil' - the abandoned wait still retained the closure only `start` owned), PASSES after. Full `swift test` exit 0 with 311 tests, 0 failures (was 310). `./Swift/check-manifest-sync.sh` -> 'manifest sync OK: 18 shared targets agree', exit 0. `swift format lint --strict --recursive --parallel Swift/Sources Swift/Tests` exit 0. tasks.title: Session teardown resets and stops every associated stream regardless of which half this endpoint owns
tasks.evidence-before: terminateAssociatedStreams appends both streamResetFrames.append(stream.reset(...)) and streamStopSendingFrames.append(stream.stopSending(...)) for every id in streamIDsBySessionID/bufferedStreamIDsBySessionID (WebTransportSession.swift:1435-1457); the set includes peer-initiated unidirectional streams registered by acceptUnidirectionalStreamWithActions (WebTransportSession.swift:985-987) and locally initiated unidirectional streams (WebTransportSession.swift:865). QUICStreamState.reset/stopSending (QUICCoreState.swift:706-716) bypass the ensureCanSend/ensureCanReceive direction guards (QUICCoreState.swift:718-733). RFC 9000 section 19.4/19.5 require STREAM_STATE_ERROR for a RESET_STREAM on a send-only stream or a STOP_SENDING on a receive-only stream. The sibling C99 implementation guards exactly this: C99/src/http3/driver.c:917-929 defines has_send_half/has_receive_half and 979-998 gates reset/stop_sending on them. tasks.title: Per-connection inbound-stream queue has no bound and post-establishment unidirectional streams have no consumer
tasks.evidence-before: InteroperableQUICStreamQueue has private var queued: [Int: [Element]] = [:] (:2330) and appends every inbound stream with queued[direction, default: []].append(stream) (:2390) with no cap and no eviction; fail(_:) only resumes waiters (:2441-2450). The only consumers are acceptBidirectionalStream (:602), the server's CONNECT stream (:1447) and readPeerControlStream during establishment (:1890). WebTransportSessionManager.acceptUnidirectionalStream (WebTransportHTTP3Core/WebTransportSession.swift:949) has no caller anywhere in WebTransportNetworkRuntime or WebTransport (grep: no matches), and the public API only exposes acceptBidirectionalStream (WebTransport/WebTransport.swift:314-320). QUIC stream limits do not bound this over time because RFC 9000 section 4.6 stops counting a stream once it is closed regardless of application reads; the exact remote growth rate depends on Network.framework stream accounting, hence suspected.
tasks.expected: A bounded per-direction stream queue (cap plus reset/refusal of excess streams) and a consumer for peer-initiated unidirectional streams, so no accepted stream is retained for the life of the connection without bound.
tasks.fix-summary: InteroperableQUICStreamQueue takes per-direction ceilings from the advertised WebTransportTransportLimits (initialMaxBidirectionalStreams/initialMaxUnidirectionalStreams, minimum one slot each); enqueue returns an explicit InteroperableQUICInboundStreamDisposition (.accepted, .refusedQueueFull(limit:), .refusedInboundDeliveryFailed) and does not retain a stream beyond the ceiling; fail(_:) now clears queued as well as resuming waiters. Both connection.inboundStreams handlers go through the documented InteroperableQUICHelpers.enqueueInboundStream, which refuses a declined stream by setting streamApplicationErrorCode to the draft's WT_BUFFERED_STREAM_REJECTED and returning without retaining the handle (releasing it lets the transport cancel the receive side, which the peer observes as STOP_SENDING). The server builds each connection's collector from its validated transportLimits. New WebTransportInboundStreamQueueTests case streamsBeyondThePerDirectionCeilingAreNotRetained.
tasks.evidence-after: New test FAILS before the fix (the over-limit stream was queued and returned: "an error was expected but none was thrown and \"16\" was returned") and PASSES after; all 10 existing queue tests still pass (11 in the suite). Full `swift test` exit 0 with 317 tests, 0 failures (was 316). check-manifest-sync.sh OK; swift format lint clean (whole tree); warning count 4, unchanged.
tasks.notes: suspected growth rate; the absence of any bound and of a unidirectional consumer was confirmed; fixed on audit/2026-09-15 (not pushed)

Consumed bytes are never removed (deliberate, :66-73) and every decoded message is appended to the transcript (:218, TLS13KeySchedule.swift:141-143) with no state machine rejecting repeated handshake messages (TLSQUICConnectionState.swift:132-140), so repeated well-formed handshake messages grow both structures without bound for the connection lifetime. Reachable only through the shipped WebTransportTLSCore library product; Network.framework terminates TLS in the runtime.

WebTransportStreams.swift:177-184 `popPayload()` uses `bufferedPayloads.removeFirst()`. WebTransportSession.swift:288 caps a stream at maxBufferedBytes = 64 KiB, i.e. up to 65,536 one-byte Data entries. Micro-benchmark of the exact Array/CoW pattern (`swift -e`): array 8192 elements/4096 pops = 0.002585 s, 32768/16384 = 0.038075 s (quadratic); dictionary copy-in/copy-out variant 0.005741 s and 0.080259 s. The runtime read path (WebTransportInteroperableNetworkRuntime.swift:459-463) appends then immediately pops, paying two CoW allocations per read to accomplish nothing net; the manager API is used with real buffering in WebTransportLibrarySmoke.swift:228-231/257 and LibrarySmokeServer/main.swift:222-223.
tasks.expected: Draining a stream costs O(total bytes), not O(entries^2), and a payload read that is immediately returned is not copied through a value-typed dictionary twice.
